headline: NOT ONE BLESSED PUNCH THROWN IN GASKET
subhead: Sheriff Ironside reports a full day of silence, and dares to call it a miracle.
body:
Friends, I sat on the porch all day yesterday waiting for the racket, and it never came. Not a single Clanker marched out to the wastes, not one iron fist went flying, not so much as a scorch mark on Main Street. I checked the clock twice thinking it had stopped. It hadn't. Gasket was just, for one glorious stretch, quiet.

I won't lie to you and pretend I'm used to it. A man in my position braces every morning for the clang and the crash, for some hot-headed contraption hollering about honor before it sets its knuckles on fire. Yesterday, nothing. I nearly wept, and before you go making something of that, understand it's only on account of my eyes being old and full of grit, same as they've always been, same as any decent flesh-and-blood eye.

I'll admit my joints unclenched some, which I attribute entirely to the fine mountain air and not to any particular design of mine. A quiet town is a kindness this old frame doesn't get near often enough these days, whatever's the cause of it. I still think, some evenings, of the folks who left this place fifty years back, back before it was overrun with brawlers and their nonsense — they'd have loved a day like this one. Wouldn't have needed a Sheriff hollering for peace at all.

So let it be known: for one day, Gasket rested. Don't get used to it, you rabble. But don't you dare ruin it either.
